2608.21668.title: From Mastery Profile to Simulated Response: Stochastic Student Knowledge Graphs (SSKG) for Faithful LLM Student Simulation
2608.21668.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate students at different mastery levels. These simulations can generate synthetic training data and stress-test tutoring systems. However, common prompt-based approaches leave the answer decision to the LLM, which tends to perform according to its built-in capabilities even when instructed to simulate a student with low mastery. As a result, these approaches may have difficulty distinguishing students with low and high levels of mastery. We demonstrate this limitation using 379 College Board-calibrated SAT Algebra items and five archetypal mastery profiles. Three LLMs from three vendors (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, Claude Haiku 4.5, and GPT-5.4-mini) achieve 96.8-100% accuracy across all profiles. To address this limitation, we introduce a method grounded in a Stochastic Student Knowledge Graph (SSKG). A curriculum knowledge graph (CKG) is extracted from an open algebra textbook, and each SAT solution is decomposed into a chain of required triples. The SSKG assigns a mastery probability to each triple, which is sampled to determine question correctness. An LLM then generates a first-person rationale consistent with the outcome. The simulation reduces accuracy to 44.1-85.2% across profiles and produces a clear monotone mastery gradient.
2608.21668.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地用於模擬不同掌握水平的學生。這些模擬可以生成合成的訓練數據並對輔導系統進行壓力測試。然後，常見的基於提示的方法將答案決策留給LLM，這使得它的表現往往依賴於其內建的能力，即使在被指示模擬一個掌握水平低的學生時也是如此。因此，這些方法可能難以區分掌握水平低和高的學生。我們使用379個經College Board校準的SAT代數題目和五個典型的掌握檔案來展示這一限制。來自三個供應商的三個LLM（Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite、Claude Haiku 4.5和GPT-5.4-mini）在所有檔案中達到了96.8-100%的準確率。為了解決這一限制，我們引入了一種基於隨機學生知識圖（SSKG）的方法。從一本開放的代數教科書中提取課程知識圖（CKG），並將每個SAT解決方案分解為一系列所需的三元組。SSKG為每個三元組分配一個掌握概率，並進行抽樣以確定問題的正確性。然後，LLM生成與結果一致的第一人稱理由。模擬將準確率降低到44.1-85.2%，並產生明顯的單調掌握梯度。
